item.title: Track that Scat! (Columbia) — Tue Nov 10, 3:30 PM
item.description:
Even when we don’t see wildlife, we can find what they leave behind! Join NCWF and Pocosin Lakes National Wildlife Refuge as we explore local species of mammals and search for the “clues” they leave on the landscape. ecoEXPLORErs will recreate examples of these clues in a creative art activity that will get them one step closer to their Mammalogy Badge! ecoEXPLORE is a community science program, created by the North Carolina Arboretum, where children of all ages are able to learn how to identify wildlife around them, help real scientists track wildlife activity, and earn fun badges and prizes all at the same time! To learn more about ecoEXPLORE, please visit https://www.ecoexplore.net/
Source: NC Wildlife Federation

item.title: Celebration of Minnie Bruce Pratt — Tue Nov 10, 5:30 PM — Smith Warehouse
item.description:
The fall issue of the Georgia Review contains a folio of material that pays tribute to the exemplary poet and poet citizen Minnie Bruce Pratt. Sinister Wisdom's editor, Julie R Enszer, worked on this folio with Taylor Marie Doherty (a former intern of Sinister Wisdom), Laura Harris, Silas Heying, and Amanda Mixon. On Tuesday, November 10 at 5:30 p.m. at Duke University, we will celebrate the work and legacies of Minnie Bruce Pratt. Join us to hear from readers and admirers of Pratt's work including Alexis Pauline Gumbs, Alexa Garvoille, Laura Harris, Silas Heying, Julie Enszer, Kelly Wooten, and more. This event will be moderated by Gerald Maa, director & editor of the Georgia Review. Light refreshments will be served. Sponsored by Sinister Wisdom, Georgia Review, and the Sallie Bingham Center. RSVPs appreciated, but registration is not required.
Source: Duke Arts, Duke University

item.title: Film Screening: "A Real Pain" — Tue Nov 10, 7:00 PM — Rubenstein Arts Center
item.description:
The Jewish Studies Course 175CNS "Holocaust Memory through the Ages: Memoirs, Memorials, Movies" screens the film "A Real Pain."
A Real Pain (2024) Directed by Jesse Eisenberg | United States/Poland | 90 min
Blending sharp humor with poignant reflection, A Real Pain follows two estranged Jewish American cousins, David (Jesse Eisenberg) and Benji (Kieran Culkin), who travel to Poland after the death of their beloved grandmother, a Holocaust survivor. Joining a Jewish heritage tour, they visit sites connected to Jewish life, memory, and the Holocaust while seeking a deeper understanding of their family's past.
As the journey unfolds, long-simmering tensions between the cousins rise to the surface. David is cautious, practical, and reserved; Benji is charismatic, impulsive, and emotionally raw. Their contrasting personalities shape both their encounters with Poland's complex history and their efforts to navigate grief, memory, and family relationships.

item.title: Anzû Quartet: Chamber Music Concert — Tue Nov 10, 7:30 PM — East Duke 201 - Nelson Music Room
item.description:
The Department of Music is pleased to present a concert by Anzû Quartet, our visiting ensemble for 2026-27.
The program includes works by Duke graduate student composers, including a song cycle by Christopher Williams "A phantom attempts to sing as she once did on earth" with soprano Clara Rottsolk. Chris's composition sets text generated through an imaginative application of AI technology, using the complete works of William Blake as source material for a large language model.
Anzû Quartet Members: Olivia de Prato, violin Ken Thomson, clarinet Ashley Bathgate, cello Karl Larson, piano
This concert is made possible through the generous support of Duke Arts and the Mary Duke Biddle Foundation.
This event is free and open to the public. No tickets are required.

ome join us in the fields to lose track of time, be outdoors, practice embodied work, and experience profound community with plants, soil, and humans! She is a Licensed Clinical Social Worker and a Certified Employee Assistance Professional, with over 15 years of experience.

item.title: UNC War Memorial Rededication Ceremony — Wed Nov 11, 2:30 PM — 140 E. Cameron Ave
item.description:
UNC-Chapel Hill will rededicate the UNC War Memorial to add names to its bronze Book of Names honoring alumni who died during service. The ceremony of rembrance, reflection and gratitude is hosted by the Carolina Veterans Alumni Network and will feature remarks from Rear Adm. Kristin Acquavella '93.
Dedicated in2007, the memorial gave Carolina its first campus site honoring alumni lost in conflicts beyond the Civil War and World War I, which Memorial Hall commemorates. The original Book of Names listed 684 alumni from the Civil War through the Gulf War and was designed with space to add names identified later.
Source: UNC Chapel Hill

item.title: Butterfly Highway Site Prep (Belmont) — Fri Nov 13, 9:00 AM
item.description:
Join North Carolina Wildlife Federation and Daniel Stowe Conservancy for a morning of Pollinator Pitstop site prep. NCWF is partnering with Daniel Stowe to conduct trials of our Butterfly Highway seed mix. These trials will inform tips and methods for site prep and seed sowing, enhance pollinator habitat, and inspire folks to take create habitat in their community. Volunteers are needed to help us prepare the sites by shoveling sod, spreading mulch, and digging edges. The morning will culminate with seed sowing of 6 plots! We will track these plots over time and document the life cycle of each species in the mix. Minimum age of 16 years to participate and accompanied by an adult if under 18. Registration is required so we can share event details and last-minute changes. REGISTER HERE

item.title: Jewish History Trolley Tours — Sun Nov 15, 1:00 PM — Mordecai Historic Park
item.description:
Take a journey to uncover Raleigh’s Jewish heritage and history, starting with Raleigh’s first Jewish resident, Moses Mordecai, the namesake of Mordecai Historic Park. We’ll learn about Michael and Regina Grausman, who hosted Raleigh’s first synagogue in their home. And new this year, each row of the trolley holds a trip packet with photos and small maps to help us explore the buildings, sites, and lives of those who built Raleigh’s Jewish community. These hour-long tours begin and end at Mordecai Historic Park at 1:00 pm, 2:00 pm and 3:00 pm. Please arrive 15 minutes early to check tickets and to meet the trolley on time. Tickets can be purchased online at reclink.raleighnc.gov or in person at the Mordecai Visitor Center. For more information, call 919-996-4364.
Source: NC Humanities Council

item.title: Foreign Policy at the AI Frontier: How AI is Reshaping Progress, Power, and Peace — Wed Nov 18, 5:30 PM — FedEx Global Education Center
item.description:
Join the Duke-UNC Rotary Peace Center on Wednesday, November 18 at the FedEx Global Education Center for the launch of Branka Panic's new book, Foreign Policy at the AI Frontier: How AI is Reshaping Progress, Power, and Peace - a comprehensive guide for anyone navigating AI's transformative impact on diplomacy and foreign policy.
Organized around three themes, the book traces how Progress and Power are being reshaped by geopolitical competition, the rise of Big Tech as quasi-sovereign actors, and threats from lethal autonomous systems to AI-driven cyber warfare — before turning to Peace, with real-world applications of AI in diplomacy, peacebuilding, and crisis management, and the Global South's growing role in shaping AI's future. Blending case studies with ethical reflection, it closes not with predictions but with aspirations: how nations might navigate AI rivalry and redirect these technologies toward peace.

item.title: Native Plants, Thriving Wildlife: Join Our Rain Garden Project! (Gatesville) — Sat Nov 21, 10:00 AM
item.description: Join NCWF Wildlife Habitat Stewards of Northeastern NC Chapter as we work together to establish a new native plant rain garden alongside the Coleman Trail. This exciting project will feature more than twenty plant species native to beautiful northeastern NC, creating a demonstration garden that showcases how native plants can transform wet or poorly drained areas into thriving wildlife habitat. Participants will also gain ideas and inspiration for managing water-prone areas in their own landscapes. Native plant rain gardens are designed to capture and filter stormwater, allowing it to slowly soak into the ground rather than running off into nearby waterways. The deep roots of native plants help reduce erosion, improve water quality, and create valuable habitat for wildlife throughout the year. item.title: Knock, Knock (Theatre for the Very Young) — Sun Nov 29, 10:00 AM — Raleigh Little Theatre
item.description:
Knock, Knock is the perfect way to kick off the holiday season with this adventure through an apartment building. Meet the various residents behind different doors and on different floors and see delivery boxes become imaginative forts, snowflake crafting causing frustrations, join a festive party, and try to keep warm in the winter chill. There are giggles and surprises behind every door, and lots of chances to get involved with the action. Created by Olivia Aston Bosworth and Samantha Provenzano Commissioned by Alliance Theatre Originally developed and produced by the Alliance Theatre (Atlanta, GA) as part of the Kathy and Ken Bernhardt Theatre for the Very Young series. Sound Elements and Composition by Multiband Studios. Dialogue complexity: no typical conversations, performers use key words that are frequently repeated and rely on physical actions and props to tell the story.

item.title: Making Our Voices Heard (America 250 NC Traveling Exhibit) — Mon Feb 8 — May Memorial Library
item.description:
This exhibit tells the stories of seven everyday North Carolinians and extraordinary leaders — Gertrude Weil, Henry Owl, Joe Lewis, Abraham Galloway, Ronald Mace, James Hunter, and Willa Player — who petitioned, protested, and organized to expand democracy. The exhibit explores change, freedom, civic responsibility, and overcoming challenges by telling the story of a few North Carolinians who have raised their voices to call out injustice and fully participate in our democratic society.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: NCMA Online Educator Course: Art and Math — Mon Feb 8
item.description:
This self-paced, ten hour course explores points of integration between the K-8 North Carolina Essential Standards in Math and Visual Art. The course includes opportunities for educators to learn strategies for using art to identify math concepts, apply math skills to create art, and to reflect within a collaborative peer learning community. Participants will gain an understanding of best practices in arts integration and will become more familiar with the North Carolina Museum of Art’s collection.
Each course module is divided into three sections: Define, Explore, and Practice. In Define, we introduce concepts, vocabulary, and works of art to stimulate thinking and help you begin identifying points of integration between art and math. In Explore, we ask you to deeply engage in those points of integration through participating in visual thinking routines and short activities that uncover math within art. item.title: Learning in Networks Reading Group — Tue Nov 10, 12:00 PM — Gross Hall
item.description:
Learning in Networks Reading Group and Seminar Series: Tuesdays, 12pm in 330 Gross Hall; lunch included The institute focuses on fundamental questions in statistical inference, machine learning, causal inference, and optimization on networks, with particular emphasis on statistical-computational tradeoffs, message-passing algorithms, learning dynamics, and network-based market design. By fostering collaboration across disciplines, the institute aims to develop new mathematical and algorithmic foundations for understanding complex networked systems and their applications. The institute is led by collaborators Jiaming Xu, Alex Belloni, Fan Wei, Galen Reeves, and James Moody. Learn more: https://sites.duke.edu/learninginnetworks/
Source: Duke University
